Memory safety, zero-cost abstractions, a.message: Memory safety, zero-cost abstractions, and high concurrency performance. Leverages Rust's ownership model for enterprise-grade reliability and efficiency.

Fully asynchronous architecture using Ru.message: Fully asynchronous architecture using Rust's async capabilities. Non-blocking design supports high-concurrency message processing with optimal resource utilization.

Supports multiple platforms including Li.message: Supports multiple platforms including Linux, Windows, and macOS. Convenient deployment across different environments with consistent performance and behavior.

homepage.arch.step.register.detail.message: Brokers register their topics with the NameServer and keep the route table fresh with heartbeats.

homepage.arch.step.discover.detail.message: Producers and consumers ask the NameServer for a topic route, then connect straight to the right Broker.

homepage.arch.step.send.detail.message: The producer picks a queue and sends asynchronously, over remoting or over gRPC through the Proxy.

homepage.arch.step.persist.detail.message: The Broker appends to the CommitLog, builds ConsumeQueue and index entries, and replicates to its slave.

homepage.arch.step.consume.detail.message: Consumers receive messages through Push, LitePull or POP, then commit offsets or acknowledge receipts.

homepage.arch.step.failover.detail.message: When a master goes down, the Raft-based Controller elects a new one from the in-sync replicas.

homepage.arch.title.message: Follow a message from producer to consumer

homepage.arch.lead.message: Route discovery, sending, persistence, replication and delivery: every hop of the RocketMQ model, implemented in async Rust.

homepage.arch.diagram.label.message: Cluster diagram: producer, NameServer, a broker group with master and slave, consumer, Controller and Proxy. The highlighted links show the selected step.

homepage.code.producer.builder.text.message: Groups, NameServer addresses and timeouts are plain builder calls on a runtime you own.

homepage.code.producer.message.text.message: A message is checked when it is built, before it ever reaches the network.

homepage.code.producer.result.text.message: Every send returns a typed result carrying the status, message ID and queue offset.

homepage.code.consumer.setup.text.message: Consumer group, start position and commit mode are all visible at the call site.

homepage.code.consumer.loop.text.message: LitePull hands you batches on your schedule. Push and POP are there when you want callbacks or receipts.

homepage.code.consumer.commit.text.message: Commit offsets only after your own processing has succeeded.

homepage.code.manifest.crates.text.message: Client, model, runtime and observability crates are released together under one version.

homepage.code.manifest.tokio.text.message: Async end to end, alongside the macros, signals and timers you already use.

homepage.code.title.message: An API that feels like Rust

homepage.code.lead.message: Builders, typed results and explicit lifecycles. No hidden threads, no surprises.

homepage.cta.title.message: Build the next generation of messaging with us

homepage.cta.lead.message: RocketMQ-Rust is developed in the open. Star the repository, join the discussion, or pick up a good first issue.

homepage.cta.disclaimer.message: RocketMQ-Rust is an independent community project, not an official Apache Software Foundation release. Apache RocketMQ is a trademark of the Apache Software Foundation.

homepage.eco.services.text.message: NameServer, Broker, Proxy and Controller: the deployable runtime of a RocketMQ cluster.

homepage.eco.libraries.text.message: Client SDK, protocol, transport, storage engines, runtime and auth, each usable on its own from crates.io.

homepage.eco.operations.text.message: Admin CLI and TUI, web and desktop dashboards, MCP servers and AI SRE workflows.

homepage.eco.title.message: One workspace, a whole messaging platform

homepage.eco.lead.message: Services, libraries and operations tooling evolve together in a single repository.

homepage.why.safety.title.message: Memory safety without a garbage collector

homepage.why.safety.text.message: Ownership and borrowing rule out data races and use-after-free at compile time. With no GC, there are no stop-the-world pauses on the message path.

homepage.why.safety.verdict.message: Caught by the compiler, not in production

homepage.why.async.text.message: Built on Tokio. Networking, request processing and background services are non-blocking, with owned runtimes and orderly shutdown.

homepage.why.protocol.text.message: Implements the remoting protocol and the gRPC messaging API, so Rust and Java clients and servers interoperate at documented boundaries.

homepage.why.storage.text.message: An append-only CommitLog with ConsumeQueue and index files, a RocksDB backend, and tiered storage for data beyond local disks.

homepage.why.patterns.text.message: Ordered, delayed, transactional, batch and request-reply messaging, consumed through Push, LitePull or POP.

homepage.why.ha.text.message: A Raft-based Controller coordinates master election and in-sync replicas across Broker groups.

homepage.why.security.text.message: Authentication, ACL authorization and TLS guard client and administrative access.

homepage.why.observability.text.message: Prometheus metrics plus OpenTelemetry traces and logs over OTLP, enabled through opt-in build features.

homepage.why.lead.message: The RocketMQ model you already know, rebuilt in a language that turns whole classes of runtime failures into compile errors.

homepage.start.clone.text.message: Fetch the workspace and build it with the pinned Rust 1.95 toolchain.

homepage.start.namesrv.text.message: The route registry for brokers and clients. It listens on 127.0.0.1:9876 by default.

homepage.start.broker.text.message: Give the Broker a home directory for its store and point it at the NameServer.

homepage.start.client.text.message: Start the consumer first, then run the producer from a second terminal.

homepage.start.lead.message: Four steps stand up a local cluster from source and push your first messages through it.

homepage.hero.lead.message: RocketMQ-Rust is a community-built Rust implementation of Apache RocketMQ: NameServer, Broker, Proxy, Controller and async clients — memory-safe, non-blocking, and speaking the RocketMQ remoting and gRPC protocols.
